A Masters in Public Health in UK can open up opportunities in epidemiology, health research, disease prevention, health policy and population health. For international students planning to study in 2027, choosing the right programme means comparing much more than university rankings.

Most full-time UK public health master's degrees take around 12 months, although some last longer. Universities offer both Master of Public Health (MPH) and MSc Public Health qualifications, with different modules, entry requirements and tuition fees.

For 2027 entry, published international tuition fees among the selected campus-based programmes in this guide range from £17,170 to £49,650.

That is a difference of more than £32,000 for courses within the same broad subject area.

This guide compares universities offering public health postgraduate degrees in the UK, alongside admission requirements, fees, scholarships, January and September intakes, and career opportunities.

If you are still deciding on a postgraduate subject, comparing different academic and career-focused courses available in the UK can help you narrow your options.

What Is a Masters in Public Health in the UK?

A master's in public health is a postgraduate qualification focused on protecting and improving the health of communities and populations.

While clinical medicine primarily concentrates on individual patients, public health investigates the wider factors that influence health outcomes. These include disease patterns, housing, nutrition, environmental conditions, healthcare access and social inequality.

Consider a city experiencing rising rates of childhood asthma.

A clinician may treat an individual child. A public health researcher might instead investigate air pollution, housing quality and neighbourhood differences to identify broader causes and recommend preventive action.

That population-level perspective is central to public health education.

UK public health master's programmes commonly cover epidemiology, biostatistics, global health, health promotion, research methods and public health policy.

Graduates from medicine, nursing, pharmacy, biological sciences, psychology, sociology and other relevant backgrounds may find suitable programmes.

MPH vs MSc Public Health: Which Degree Should You Choose?

Both an MPH and an MSc Public Health can provide advanced knowledge of population health. The distinction depends more on the individual programme than on its title.

These differences are not universal. An MPH can be highly quantitative, while an MSc may emphasise practical community health interventions.

Here's the thing: two programmes with similar names can provide noticeably different training.

If you enjoy analysing disease patterns, look for strong epidemiology and biostatistics modules. If your interests involve community wellbeing or health policy, examine health promotion, intervention design and policy evaluation.

For a more research-intensive academic route, you may also consider postgraduate qualifications centred on independent research.

Several British universities offer postgraduate public health programmes, ranging from specialist research-focused degrees to multidisciplinary courses examining health inequalities and social policy.

The following comparison uses published university information for 2027 entry wherever available.

Fee information: Published amounts relate to 2027/28 entry and the specified full-time options. Manchester has not yet published its 2027 fee; its 2026/27 international fee was £29,900. The UCL programme listed here is distance learning. Individual fees and course details may change.

1. City St George's, University of London

City St George's offers an MPH covering epidemiology, health policy, health improvement, health protection and research methods.

Students can choose between in-person teaching at its Clerkenwell campus and online delivery.

The course normally takes one year full-time or two years part-time. Its published 2027/28 international tuition fee is £17,170 for the full-time MPH.

Applicants generally need at least a recognised 2:2 degree or equivalent. Relevant health-sector experience is also considered.

The university lists September 2027 and January 2028 start dates, although applications for the 2027/28 course are not yet open.

For students seeking a comparatively affordable London-based MPH, it is an option worth investigating.

2. University of Surrey

Surrey offers a one-year MSc Public Health starting in September 2027.

The programme draws on health sciences, psychology, biosciences and evidence-based approaches to population health.

Its curriculum includes topics such as health behaviour, disease prevention, research and health inequalities.

The published international fee is £19,300, with a typical minimum academic requirement of a relevant 2:2 degree.

Surrey may suit applicants who want a multidisciplinary public health qualification with an emphasis on research-informed practice.

3. Sheffield Hallam University

Sheffield Hallam's MSc Public Health takes 18 months full-time and costs £19,530 for international students in 2027/28.

Its approach connects public health with sociology, social policy and the wider determinants of wellbeing.

Students examine how education, urban planning, workplaces, transport and social conditions affect population health.

The university accepts applicants from varied academic backgrounds and considers relevant public health or research experience.

September 2027 and January 2028 starts are listed.

4. University College London

UCL offers a Master of Public Health through distance learning.

The programme includes public health research, policy, population health challenges and practical approaches to improving health outcomes.

Its curriculum is validated by the Agency for Public Health Education Accreditation (APHEA).

For September 2027 entry, the full-time online MPH costs £20,500 and takes one calendar year. Part-time and flexible study options are also available.

One detail is easy to miss: this is an online programme, not an equivalent campus-based London course.

That makes study mode an important consideration, particularly for applicants comparing the overall experience of different universities.

5. Loughborough University

Loughborough's MSc Public Health explores health inequalities, population health and the social and environmental factors influencing wellbeing.

The programme starts in September 2027 and normally takes one year full-time.

International tuition is £25,750 for 2027/28.

Applicants typically need a relevant 2:2 honours degree or equivalent, although the university may consider applicants with other qualifications and appropriate professional experience.

Loughborough may appeal to students interested in community health, public health evidence and reducing health inequalities.

6. University of Liverpool

Liverpool's MPH combines epidemiology, public health statistics, health improvement, research methods and health policy.

The programme takes 12 months full-time, with September 2027 entry.

Its current published international tuition fee is £33,000 for 2027/28.

Applicants generally need a recognised degree at 2:2 level or above, together with evidence of relevant public health experience. The university also considers some applicants through alternative experience-based routes.

Liverpool is particularly relevant for students interested in connecting research evidence with public health practice and policy.

7. Imperial College London

Imperial offers a one-year MPH starting in October 2027.

The programme places considerable emphasis on epidemiology, quantitative methods, biostatistics and public health research.

It may appeal to applicants with a strong scientific or medical background who want advanced analytical training.

The international tuition fee for 2027 entry is £49,650.

Imperial is the highest-priced university in this comparison, so applicants should assess the course content and total cost against their academic goals.

8. University of Manchester

Manchester offers a campus-based MPH lasting one year full-time.

The programme explores public health practice, research and interdisciplinary topics, with opportunities to study areas such as global health, health economics and planetary health.

Its 2027 tuition fee has not yet been confirmed. For reference, the international fee for the September 2026 academic year was £29,900.

Manchester may suit health professionals and graduates interested in a broad public health qualification with specialist study options.

The right university depends on what you want to learn, not simply where it appears in a league table.

Masters in Public Health in UK Fees and Cost of Study

Tuition fees for public health master's programmes vary substantially by university, location, duration and delivery mode.

Among the selected 2027 campus-based courses above:

  • City St George's charges £17,170.
  • Surrey charges £19,300.
  • Loughborough charges £25,750.
  • Liverpool charges £33,000.
  • Imperial charges £49,650.

These are programme-specific figures, not a definitive UK-wide minimum or maximum.

Which Universities Offer More Affordable Public Health Masters?

City St George's, Surrey and Sheffield Hallam have comparatively lower published tuition fees within this shortlist.

However, affordability goes beyond the course fee.

Students attending university in person should consider accommodation, transport, food, learning materials and personal expenses. Costs can differ substantially between London, Sheffield, Liverpool and other locations.

For example, a £17,170 course in London may not necessarily result in the lowest overall study budget if accommodation is considerably more expensive.

Some students may find that a slightly higher tuition fee at a university in a more affordable location works better for their circumstances.

Comparing lower-priced postgraduate programmes across the UK can provide useful context before finalising a shortlist.

MPH in UK Eligibility and Entry Requirements

Admission requirements vary by university, but applicants generally need a recognised undergraduate qualification and must meet the programme's English language standards.

Academic Requirements

Relevant degree backgrounds commonly include:

  • Medicine, dentistry and nursing
  • Pharmacy and allied health sciences
  • Biology and biomedical sciences
  • Public health and environmental sciences
  • Psychology and sociology
  • Statistics and other relevant disciplines

A UK 2:1 or 2:2 honours degree, or an accepted international equivalent, is common.

For example, Surrey normally requires at least a 2:2 in a relevant subject. Liverpool considers graduates from health-related and other disciplines at 2:2 level or above, with relevant experience.

City St George's also publishes country-specific qualification equivalencies. For certain eligible Bangladeshi degrees, its guidance indicates that a GPA of 3.0/4.0 may correspond to a UK 2:2. Qualification type, university and award date can affect that assessment.

Applicants should therefore check their own university's country-specific standards rather than assume every UK institution uses the same conversion.

Medical graduates who are comparing academic postgraduate education with clinical training may benefit from exploring different study routes available after completing an MBBS.

Is Work Experience Necessary?

Not always.

Some MPH programmes expect experience relevant to population health, particularly when designed for practising professionals. Other MSc programmes focus more heavily on previous academic qualifications.

Experience may include healthcare employment, public health research, community projects, internships or volunteering.

A psychology graduate who helped evaluate a community mental health initiative, for instance, could have experience relevant to public health even without a clinical qualification.

What matters is whether the work demonstrates skills and understanding that fit the course.

What Subjects Are Covered in a UK Public Health Masters?

Most MPH and MSc Public Health programmes bring together several disciplines.

Epidemiology examines how diseases and health conditions are distributed across populations. It helps researchers identify patterns, causes and risk factors.

Biostatistics involves analysing health data, interpreting research results and applying statistical methods to public health questions.

Health promotion focuses on improving wellbeing through prevention, community engagement and evidence-based interventions.

Health policy and management explores how organisations design, implement and evaluate health strategies.

Global health considers international health challenges, including infectious diseases, inequalities, environmental risks and health-system performance.

Research methods and dissertation work allow students to investigate a specific problem in greater depth.

For example, a student could evaluate whether a school nutrition programme reduces childhood obesity, while another might investigate geographical differences in access to cancer screening.

The strongest course choice depends on which subjects connect most closely with your interests.

Students can compare the usual autumn university admission timetable when organising their application plans.

January and May 2027 Intake

January 2027 options are more limited, but they do exist.

The University of Chester lists January and May 2027 starts for its Master of Public Health programme.

Its published international fee is £15,500 for the 2026/27 academic year, which covers those listed starts. This must not be confused with a confirmed September 2027 fee.

Sheffield Hallam also lists January 2027 for its 2026/27 MSc Public Health programme, with international tuition of £18,600 for that academic year.

By contrast, its next academic-year listing includes January 2028.

That distinction matters. Searching for “MPH January intake 2027” does not mean every university page labelled 2027 offers a January start.

For wider options, compare universities offering courses early in the calendar year and verify the specific public health programme.

University Scholarships

Loughborough publishes an Excellence Scholarship worth £6,000 off tuition fees for eligible international students.

The award generally requires a first-class degree or international equivalent, together with the scholarship's other conditions.

The university also lists an alumni discount worth up to £3,000 for eligible September 2027 entrants.

Applicants should confirm whether awards can be combined before estimating any reduction in tuition.

Commonwealth Master's Scholarships

The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission provides scholarships for eligible candidates from specified low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries.

For the 2027/28 academic year, the published application closing date is 20 October 2026 at 16:00 BST.

The scheme supports qualifying one-year full-time taught master's programmes. It is not automatically available for every MPH course, particularly longer or distance-learning routes.

The Commission's published benefits include approved tuition fees, eligible travel costs and a monthly living allowance. The currently stated stipend is £1,712 per month, or £2,000 for scholars studying in the London metropolitan area, subject to the award's conditions.

Candidates must also meet academic, nationality, residency and selection requirements.

Chevening Scholarships

Chevening Scholarships fund eligible one-year master's study for selected applicants from participating countries.

The 2027/28 application round is already closed for Bangladesh and India, although availability and deadlines may differ elsewhere.

Students should consult their country-specific scholarship page before planning an application.

Those looking for additional awards can explore scholarships available to applicants from Bangladesh, including opportunities with different selection criteria.

Scholarships are competitive, so they should be treated as possibilities rather than assumed reductions in the cost of studying.

Career Opportunities After a Masters in Public Health in UK

A public health master's develops analytical, research and policy-related skills that can be relevant across healthcare, research organisations, charities and government-linked services.

Potential career directions include:

Public Health Research Officer

Epidemiology-related researcher

Study disease patterns and population-level risks

Public Health Programme Coordinator

Support and evaluate health programmes

Employers may include NHS organisations, local authorities, universities, research institutes, charities and international health organisations.

Does an MPH Lead Directly to Public Health Specialist Registration?

No.

Some specialist posts require recognised specialty training, substantial professional experience and registration with an appropriate body.

The UK Public Health Register identifies separate routes to specialist registration, including approved specialty training and portfolio assessment.

An MPH can contribute valuable knowledge, but the degree alone does not confer specialist registration or authorise clinical practice.

How to Choose the Right Public Health Masters in UK

Start with your intended career direction.

If you enjoy data analysis, prioritise courses with epidemiology, biostatistics and quantitative research. If you want to work in community health or policy, examine health promotion, health inequalities and programme evaluation.

Then compare three practical factors.

First, check academic suitability. A highly specialised course may require knowledge or experience you have not yet developed.

Second, look at delivery and duration. A one-year campus MPH provides a different learning environment from UCL's online programme or Sheffield Hallam's 18-month course.

Third, calculate the full study budget, not just the university's headline tuition fee.

A student interested in public health policy may ultimately find a moderately priced course with relevant modules more useful than a costly programme selected mainly for its reputation.

Choose the programme that fits the work you want to do.

How to Apply for a Masters in Public Health in UK

Most universities accept postgraduate applications through their own online admissions portals.

The process generally involves:

  1. Shortlisting suitable programmes. Compare modules, entry requirements, duration and published tuition fees.
  2. Checking academic eligibility. Review university-specific criteria and international qualification equivalencies.
  3. Preparing documents. Common requirements include degree certificates, academic transcripts, references and English language evidence where applicable.
  4. Writing a personal statement. Explain your academic interests, relevant experience and reasons for studying public health. You can improve this section by understanding how to communicate your motivation and academic goals effectively.
  5. Submitting your university application. Follow the institution's instructions and published deadlines.
  6. Reviewing the university's decision. Read any offer conditions carefully, including academic requirements, fees and acceptance arrangements.

Universities make their own admissions decisions and may change programme details before the course begins.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a Masters in Public Health in UK worth it?

It can be valuable for graduates who want to develop skills in epidemiology, health research, disease prevention, policy or programme evaluation. Its value depends on the university, course content, tuition fees, previous qualifications and intended career. An MPH does not guarantee employment or a particular salary.

Can I study MPH in UK without an MBBS?

Yes. Many UK public health master's programmes accept graduates from nursing, pharmacy, biological sciences, psychology, sociology and other appropriate disciplines. Some also consider applicants with relevant professional experience. An MBBS is not a universal requirement.

Which universities offer affordable MPH courses in UK?

Among the selected 2027 campus-based programmes, City St George's lists international tuition of £17,170, Surrey £19,300 and Sheffield Hallam £19,530. These are examples of comparatively lower published fees, not a definitive ranking of the cheapest MPH courses in Britain.

What IELTS score is required for MPH in UK?

Requirements differ. Surrey normally asks for IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in each component, while Liverpool requires 7.0 overall with no component below 6.5. Some universities accept alternative English language qualifications.

Is there a January 2027 intake for Masters in Public Health in UK?

Yes. Chester and Sheffield Hallam list January 2027 options under their 2026/27 academic-year courses. Most universities in the main 2027 comparison begin in September or October. Always verify the precise start date for the programme you want.

Can international students study MPH online in UK?

Yes. UCL offers a distance-learning MPH with a one-year full-time option. City St George's also lists online delivery. Students should compare teaching schedules, assessment arrangements, equipment requirements and course suitability before choosing online study.

How long does a public health masters take in UK?

Many full-time programmes take 12 months. Sheffield Hallam's MSc Public Health takes 18 months, while part-time programmes may take two years or longer. Duration varies by university and study mode.

Are there scholarships for MPH in UK?

Yes, although eligibility varies. Examples include university awards, Chevening and Commonwealth Master's Scholarships. Applicants must check nationality rules, programme eligibility, academic conditions and deadlines. Not every scholarship covers every public health master's course.

Final Thoughts on Masters in Public Health in UK

A Masters in Public Health in UK can be a valuable step towards work in population health, research, disease prevention and public health policy. However, the strongest choice is not necessarily the university with the highest ranking or tuition fee.

For 2027 entry, universities such as City St George's, Surrey, Liverpool, Loughborough, Imperial, Manchester, Sheffield Hallam and UCL offer different approaches to public health education. Their courses vary in academic focus, duration, study mode, cost and entry requirements.

A sensible decision starts with your interests. Compare the modules you want to study, check whether your qualifications meet the entry criteria and consider the total cost alongside the experience each programme offers.

If you would like to discuss suitable UK university options based on your academic background and goals, you can speak with an education adviser about course selection and university admissions.

Choose a programme for the skills it will help you develop, not simply the name on the degree certificate.
